title: Point the statusline template at .bee/bin/bee and guard it with a test
action:
THE BUG, already reproduced. packages/bee/statusline/statusline-command.sh:66-73 hunts the bee binary with SELF_DIR=$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}") and the four candidates "$SELF_DIR/../bee", "$SELF_DIR/../bee.exe", "$SELF_DIR/../../bee", "$SELF_DIR/../../bee.exe". The script is vendored into a host at <repo>/.claude/statusline-command.sh, so SELF_DIR is <repo>/.claude and those candidates resolve to <repo>/bee, <repo>/bee.exe, <repo>/../bee, <repo>/../bee.exe. The vendored binary is at <repo>/.bee/bin/bee. Nothing matches, usage_seg stays empty, and the per-model token/cost line is dropped in silence, exit 0. HISTORY, so you do not re-introduce it: 09286b47 added the SELF_DIR loop to the template while a `node statusline-usage.mjs` fallback still stood behind it and masked the miss; 00a8fdf4 (R6 cutover) deleted that fallback AND fixed the vendored .claude copy to the CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR form, but left the canonical template on the broken loop. The two files have been out of sync since, violating onboarding R4 (canonical and vendored copies must be byte-identical), and the byte-equality sweep that would have caught it lived in packages/bee/tests/test_lib.mjs, which the same cutover deleted. NOTE the canonical file is the ONLY real edit site: onboard/plan.rs:537-546 + apply.rs:372-378 re-vendor canonical over .claude/statusline-command.sh on every `bee onboard --apply`, and devtools/mod.rs:141-149 makes `bee dev regen` run that apply, so any hand-edit of the .claude copy alone is erased.

FIX 1 -- the lookup. In packages/bee/statusline/statusline-command.sh replace the SELF_DIR candidate loop with the SAME resolver shape the hook commands already use and that hooks_wiring.rs:680-683 asserts, adapted to shell: try "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.bee/bin/bee" and its .exe first; then derive the repo from git -- g=$(git -C "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null) -- and try "$g/../.bee/bin/bee" and its .exe, which is what makes a linked worktree resolve to the MAIN checkout's binary; then `command -v bee` as the last resort. Set BEE to the first executable candidate, then usage_seg=$(echo "$input" | "$BEE" dev statusline 2>/dev/null). Keep the leg silenced and optional: a statusline must never be why a prompt fails to render, so no candidate found must still exit 0 and still print line one. Change nothing else in the file.

FIX 2 -- re-sync. Copy the corrected canonical file over .claude/statusline-command.sh so the two are byte-identical (R4).

FIX 3 -- the guard, and this is the part that stops the next regression. Add packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/statusline_contract.rs modelled on tests/installer_contracts.rs: same repo_root()/read() helpers, same 'WHY THIS FILE EXISTS' header, which must name that both guards this file restores died with the Node tree (packages/bee/tests/test_lib.mjs byte-equality sweep, and no test ever ran the script at all). Two tests: (a) canonical_and_vendored_statusline_are_byte_identical -- compare packages/bee/statusline/statusline-command.sh and .claude/statusline-command.sh as BYTES, restoring R4's sweep; (b) statusline_reaches_the_bee_binary -- #[cfg(unix)] -- build a tempdir host containing .claude/statusline-command.sh (the real canonical file copied in) and an executable .bee/bin/bee stub shell script that echoes a known marker, run `bash <tmp>/.claude/statusline-command.sh` with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<tmp> and a minimal statusline JSON payload on stdin, and assert the marker is in stdout AND the exit status is 0. Add a third if it is cheap: the same fixture with the stub REMOVED still exits 0 and still prints the first line.

PROOF ORDER, required: run test (b) against the UNFIXED template first, capture that RED output, and put it in the cap's verification_evidence -- it is the evidence that the guard actually catches this bug. Then apply FIX 1 and 2 and show it green. REGEN, required and NOT optional here: packages/bee is a release-manifest root, so after FIX 1 run the full chain in order -- bee dev regen (render-skill-trees, then onboard --repo-root . --apply, then release-manifest --write). Step 2 of that chain is what performs FIX 2 for you: onboard --apply re-vendors the corrected canonical file over .claude/statusline-command.sh. Commit the regenerated docs/history/codex-harness-hardening/release-manifest.json with the rest. Do NOT touch the onboard vendoring code, the Rust dev statusline renderer, or any other script -- the stale pointers and the stale comment in devtools/statusline.rs belong to sbl-2.
verify: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test statusline_contract && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

truths: packages/bee/statusline/statusline-command.sh finds the binary at <repo>/.bee/bin/bee for a copy vendored at <repo>/.claude/, with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set and via the git-common-dir leg when it is unset
A test asserts that byte-identity and fails if either file is edited alone
A test executes the real script against a stub binary and asserts the usage segment reaches stdout -- proven by its RED output against the unfixed template, recorded on the cap
The script still exits 0 and still prints the first line when no binary is found anywhere
